subject: RE: ACME integration — rate limits, auth, and retry strategy
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: ACME integration — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan:

Summary
- Primary use: customer support assistant + reranking for search results using embeddings.
- Expected qps: ~20 requests/sec for generation routes, embedding batch jobs ~2000 vectors/day.
- SLOs: p95 latency target 300ms for short prompts; offline rerank can be longer.

Immediate next steps
1) Tech contact: please confirm who on your infra/APIs team we should loop in for the architecture deep-dive.
2) I attached the SDK quickstart and a draft rate-limits matrix for your traffic profile (redwood-sdk-setup.pdf, acme-rate-limits-matrix.xlsx).
3) We'll propose a short architecture review to go over auth, routing, and retry behavior (30–45m).

Notes on scope for the architecture review (so we can pre-prepare):
- SDK setup & auth: service account vs API key, rotation, RBAC.
- Routing & model variants: region pinning and fallback rules.
- Structured output/tool calling: if you need deterministic JSON outputs or tool calls we can show examples.
- Embeddings & rerankers: batching, caching, and index pipeline.
- Rate limits & retries: quota model, 429 handling, idempotency best practices.

Would you be able to share the primary infra contact? Also suggest a couple of times for the architecture call next week.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
---
Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf (PDF guide), acme-rate-limits-matrix.xlsx (Excel)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acmecorp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME integration — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Ben — this is helpful.

Quick clarifying question before we schedule the architecture review: on retries and 429 handling, we need a recommended approach for idempotency and request IDs. Our infra team is strict about duplicate side-effects for generation calls that trigger downstream ticket creation. What's your guidance for: backoff strategy, safe idempotency keys (we generally use X-Request-ID headers), and whether Redwood SDK surfaces helpers for this?

Also looping in Tom (platform) to confirm times.

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Customer Experience, Acme Corp
Samantha.Lee@acmecorp.com

Thanks Ben — adding a couple of proposed mutual action plan (MAP) items so we can move quickly:

- Week 2: SDK integration + test plan (we can provide a sandbox API key).
